sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Random Forest (python-random-forest) is a risk tier 3 classifier that predicts the target variable default.payment.next.month, using the public UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 records of credit-card clients in Taiwan, April to September 2005). Its business purpose is recorded, as an inferred field, as a benchmark model for internal analysis that is not used in decisions, and it is described as a supporting comparison model rather than the migration target. The business owner, intended business use, model version and approval status are not documented.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with n_estimators=150, random_state set by a seed (default 42), n_jobs=-1 and class_weight="balanced" to handle class imbalance, with no input scaling. Data is loaded either through the official ucimlrepo client (which checks shape, missing values and default rate) or from an Excel workbook (header=1, target renamed, ID dropped, rows with missing values removed). The target is cast to int, and a stratified train/test split is applied with test_size=0.2 and random_state=42. ID, SEX and AGE are excluded from the predictors, with SEX and AGE reserved for fairness analysis; the 21 listed input features, the 0.8 train fraction and the 0.5 decision threshold are inferred fields rather than confirmed specifications.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: Hyperparameters other than n_estimators and class_weight use library defaults, no tuning is shown, and the selection rationale is not documented. The feature set depends on which loader is used (the demo fixture yields only three predictors), and the loader used in production is not documented. The UCI data is public demonstration data and not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio. Performance metrics, validation results, fairness results for SEX and AGE groups, prediction PSI, the approved decision threshold and its justification, and a monitoring plan are all not documented.
